title: Open problem: p-entropic matroids linear for prime p
statement_text: Our results leave open the possibility for $p$-entropic matroids to be linear whenever $p$ is prime.
context_text: For a positive integer $q$, a matroid $M$ on ground set $[m]$ with rank function $r$ is $q$-entropic if there is a probability distribution $\mu$ on $[q]^m$ (equivalently, random variables $X_1,\dots,X_m$ each with support of size at most $q$) such that $r(S)=H(\mu_S)$ for every $S\subseteq[m]$, where $\mu_S$ is the marginal of $\mu$ on the coordinates in $S$ and $H$ is the Shannon entropy in base $q$; so the joint entropies of the variables must all be integers and equal to the ranks. Here linear means representable over the field $\mathbb{F}_p$. Every $\mathbb{F}$-representable matroid is $|\mathbb{F}|$-entropic (take $X=AY$ for a representing matrix $A$ and a uniform random vector $Y$), and the question is whether the converse holds. The authors prove that, for every $p$, being $p$-entropic is equivalent to being a secret-sharing matroid with ground set of size $p$ (equivalently, an almost affine matroid with alphabet size $p$) and is closed under taking minors; that $p$-entropic matroids are exactly the $\mathbb{F}_p$-representable ones for $p=2$ and $p=3$; and, by a known example, that this fails for $p=9$ (there is a 9-entropic matroid representable over no field). For prime $p$ they make partial progress: every $p$-entropic matroid of rank at most two is $\mathbb{F}_p$-linear, the uniform matroid $U_{2,p+2}$ is not $p$-entropic, and the Fano plane is not $p$-entropic for $p>2$. This is a matroid-theory question.
